subject.title: [Feature]: Automatic Output Sanitization for Sensitive Data

question: Should OpenClaw add automatic sensitive-value sanitization to final user-visible agent outputs as a core security boundary, or keep core limited to current log/tool/transcript redaction plus plugin hooks?
rationale: Source inspection proves the gap, but the fix changes visible output semantics, security expectations, and likely config defaults; automation cannot choose the false-positive policy or core/plugin ownership boundary.

options.title: Approve narrow core sanitizer
options.body: Define an opt-in or explicitly scoped core output policy using existing redaction helpers, with schema, docs, tests, and false-positive/reporting behavior.

options.title: Route through plugins
options.body: Use reply_payload_sending or message_sending hooks for optional sanitizer packages if maintainers want core to stay limited to generic delivery seams.

options.title: Declare current boundary sufficient
options.body: Document logs, transcripts, diagnostics, tool payloads, and plugin hooks as the supported redaction boundary, then close or narrow this request.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow core sanitizer
recommendation.body: Define an opt-in or explicitly scoped core output policy using existing redaction helpers, with schema, docs, tests, and false-positive/reporting behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the CODEOWNERS-routed security boundary most directly responsible for credential and sensitive-output policy.
